blocks.x: What Data Engineering & Pipeline Modernization looks like when it has to survive an audit: scoped deliverables, weekly evidence, named control owners and a committed delta per gate.

Aging pipelines fail silently: silent nulls, schema drift, duplicated truth. We modernize the estate onto a medallion architecture — bronze ingestion with schema contracts, silver governed conformance, gold decision-grade marts — implemented on Databricks, Snowflake or dbt-based stacks. Every pipeline ships with data contracts, expectations testing, lineage and freshness SLAs, so consumers see reliability as a measured property, not a promise.

The program includes the unglamorous debt: source-system inventory, duplicate-pipeline consolidation, backfill strategy, and cost-per-pipeline telemetry. Clients typically consolidate 30-50% of pipelines, cut batch windows by more than half, and establish incident classes with named owners — the operational maturity that AI programs silently depend on.

Below is the delivery cadence for this capability — the same pattern on every engagement. Weeks 1–2 belong to measurement: the baseline metric is captured with your team and signed before build starts. Weeks 3–8 run a bounded pilot — one decision path, one workflow, one plant or one portfolio — steered by a control owner on your side. Weeks 9–12 convert the pilot into runbooks, monitoring and enablement, and close with a measured delta against the signed baseline. Anything that misses a gate is stopped or redirected on the record.
